Desensitisation should be regarded as temporary, and allergic reactions may recur during the next exposure to penicillin. Neutropenia. Neutropenia has been widely reported in patients given high doses of beta lactams and an inci- dence of from 5 to more than 15% has been reported in patients treated for 10 days or more. Warning signs in- clude fever, rash, and eosinophilia. Monitoring of the leucocyte count is recommended during long-term treatment with high doses. Some have proposed a di- rect toxic effect whereas others have postulated an im- mune mechanism. Effects on the blood. References to neutropenia associated with penicillins. 1. Anonymous.
